# Independent audit of the all-dimensional additive far-tail reserve

Source: `candidate 669694f08be75bf9`.


The linear shear has determinant one, preserves the longitudinal
functional, and commutes with Minkowski addition. Retaining the fixed
transverse coordinate of S avoids an affine-translation ambiguity.

For a polytope B, every vertex of its transverse projection has an
actual lift in B. Unique-support regions cover the transverse space
up to finitely many hyperplanes, null for the d-volume of the bounded
tail. The translated pieces lie in the tested halfspace by their
actual lifted heights. Their projected support gap is exactly |v|^2,
so each is outside the entire projection cylinder of S+B. The
monotonicity calculation has the correct sign and proves disjointness
of all images. Piecewise translations preserve their total volume.
No overlapping gains are counted twice and no selected point leaves
A+B.

The approximation for arbitrary B is also complete. A common interior
ball of the increasing inscribed polytopes supplies the displayed
homothety inclusion. Convexity of the fixed A and S supplies the two
corresponding inclusions of Minkowski sums. Their missing TOTAL
volumes tend to zero, which bounds the missing volume of every fixed
cap. No optimizers, normals, or centers vary in this limit. Closed
halfspaces cause no missing boundary term.

The box family proves sharpness of coefficient1 as an infimum. The
d=1 failure is explicit and consistent with the proof's transverse
dimension requirement. The mixed-fiber factor2^d is the exact
continuous midpoint Jacobian, not a parity or ambient-volume factor.

The source's normal-cone map also suggests a stronger Hausdorff-measure
version using finite support approximation with a uniform distance gap.
That separate extension is not needed to validate the audited theorem.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
